0x60525b0.model: 501-byte IOStatus Pad(uint64_t size, Env::IOPriority priority) (sret 16-byte out-pointer in rdi, WritableFileWriter* in rsi, size in rdx, priority in ecx). Seen-error gate (0x60525d5): byte this+0x89 set -> return IOStatus code 5 'Writer has previous error.' (27-byte heap state_, old sret state_ delete[]'d first), nothing else touched. Zero-fill loop (0x60525e4..0x60526c4): the entry cursize_ (this+0x58) is saved at rsp+0x8 (the pad start) and the remaining size is filled in chunks of min(buf_.capacity_ (this+0x50) - buf_.cursize_, remaining): memset (buf_.bufstart_ (this+0x60) + buf_.cursize_, 0, chunk) via the PLT memset at 0x63f0a90, cursize_ += chunk, remaining -= chunk. When remaining is still non-zero the buffer is full, so the routine calls Flush(priority) at 0x6051a20 (call site 0x605269a) with a 16-byte sret at rsp+0x10; on a non-OK Flush status (code byte at 0x10(%rsp) != 0) it sets seen_error_ = 1 and returns that status at once (0x6052758, move-assigned into the out sret with byte 2 forced to 0 -- pending_sync_ NOT set, filesize_ NOT advanced). On success it delete[]s the Flush sret state_ when non-null, reloads cursize_/capacity_ and loops. A zero-size Pad skips the loop entirely (0x60525fa). Epilogue (0x605262e): pending_sync_ (this+0x88) = 1; filesize_ (this+0x70) += size. Verification arm (0x6052641..0x605274f): only when perform_data_verification_ (this+0xd1) is set, buffered_data_crc32c_checksum_ (this+0xd4) = crc32c::Extend(checksum, buf_.bufstart_ + ENTRY cursize_, size) through the 0x61c25f0 dispatch thunk -- the pointer is the SAVED entry cursize, not the final one. When no Flush intervened the span is exactly the zeros just written; when a Flush DID intervene (size exceeded the free space at entry) the span runs past the buffer's capacity -- the binary reads heap bytes past the allocation, so the resulting checksum is NOT pinned by this model (recorded as null with the pointer/length). buffered_data_with_checksum_ (this+0xd8) is NOT consulted here (unlike Flush's WriteDirectWithChecksum selection). OK return (0x605264f): sret = {code 0, state_ null}. Direct I/O note: Pad's binary has no use_direct_io() check (upstream asserts !use_direct_io()); with direct I/O and pending_sync_ clear, Flush skips the write, the buffer stays full and the loop makes no progress -- the binary does not terminate for size > free space in that configuration. The model raises instead of hanging.

observations: The verification Extend pointer is the ENTRY cursize_, not the final one: the binary saves cursize_ at rsp+0x8 before the loop (0x60525f2) and adds bufstart_ to that saved value at 0x6052737..0x605273f. When no Flush intervened, entry cursize_ + size == final cursize_, so the span is exactly the zeros just written; the pointer arithmetic is only observable when a Flush intervened.

When a Flush intervened, the Extend reads past the buffer's capacity: entry cursize_ + size > capacity_ by construction (a Flush happens exactly when size exceeded the free space). The first (capacity_ - entry cursize_) bytes are the first chunk's zeros -- still in the buffer because AlignedBuffer::Clear only resets cursize_ -- and the rest is heap memory past the allocation. The model records the pointer/length and nulls the checksum instead of inventing bytes; the file bytes and the pending_sync_/filesize_ effects are still exact.

Every mid-loop Flush resets buffered_data_crc32c_checksum_ to 0 (the WriteBuffered[WithChecksum] contract from #6057), so a flush-intervened pad's verification Extend starts from 0, not from the entry checksum -- and the entry checksum is lost even before the over-read. The model implements this through the Flush oracle; the pinned rows (no flush) start from the entry checksum.

Pad's verification arm tests ONLY perform_data_verification_ (+0xd1). buffered_data_with_checksum_ (+0xd8) is not consulted -- unlike Flush's WriteDirectWithChecksum selection, which requires both flags. Both flags are exercised independently in the verification group.
A full buffer at entry flushes first: chunk 0, Flush, then the pad. The chunk-0 iteration is pinned in the cases (pad_chunks [0, ...]) and in the tests.

Direct I/O + pending_sync_ clear does not terminate: Flush skips the write, the buffer stays full, the loop repeats with chunk 0 forever. The binary has no use_direct_io() check in Pad (upstream asserts !use_direct_io()); the model raises ValueError on the no-progress iteration instead of hanging, and no generated case uses direct I/O.

The sole caller computes the pad size, not Pad: WriteMaybeCompressedBlock pads with (block_size - ((offset + 5) % block_size)) % block_size (block trailer: 1 type byte + 4 CRC bytes), so the next block starts aligned. The alignment math is pinned in the bindings group for block sizes 4096..65536.

Pad.cold is unwind-only (44 B): the single tail jump at 0x60527a0 is the FDE's exception landing-pad tail. The seen-error gate's delete[] guard reads the sret state_ slot after the binary zeroed it (0x60526dc), exactly as in Append/Flush -- the delete never fires on that path; the shape is described the same way as the sibling packets.
The zero-size path skips the loop but still sets pending_sync_ = 1 and runs the verification Extend with length 0 (Extend(crc, ptr, 0) == crc -- checksum unchanged).
unknowns: The bool at this+0xd9, read into both finish events by the Flush oracle: it is not named by the Append packet's writer layout and no upstream header in the 2019 mirror has a member at that offset. Modelled as flag_d9, carried into the event dicts, and listed here as an open unknown (shared with the Flush packet).

The listener method name for vtable slot 47: the slot is the binary's observed position and the FileOperationType values (4/7) plus the rocksdbjni 9.0.0 docs support OnFileFlushFinish / OnFileRangeSyncFinish for slots 35/37, but slot 47's method name is not established. Recorded as open; no name is asserted.

The heap bytes the verification Extend reads when a Flush intervened (past the buffer capacity): unpinned by design -- the model records the pointer/length and nulls the checksum rather than asserting heap contents.

Direct-I/O Pad behaviour beyond the no-progress observation: the binary's Flush handles the direct arm (WriteDirect when pending_sync_ is set), but upstream asserts !use_direct_io() for Pad, so the direct path is implemented in the Flush oracle but no Pad case uses it; the pending_sync_-clear non-termination is documented, not exercised as a case.

Flush, WriteBuffered, WriteBufferedWithChecksum, WriteDirect, WriteDirectWithChecksum and the RangeSync member are taken as oracles here (their bodies are separate FDEs; only Pad/.cold are census-bound in this packet). Their internal steps are modelled from the #6057/#6041 contracts and upstream source, not from their own binary bodies in this packet; the Write* routines are the natural follow-ups.
